G2220957.description: Yaoundé (UK: ; US: , French pronunciation: [ja.unde]) is the capital city of Cameroon. It has a population of more than 2.8 million, which makes it the second-largest city in the country after the port city Douala.

G2221030.description: Yagoua is a town and commune in the Far North Province of Cameroon. It is the capital of the department of Mayo-Danay.

G2221513.description: Tignère is a town and commune in Cameroon.

G2221607.description: Tcholliré is a town and commune in Cameroon.

G2222230.description: Sangmélima is a town on the Lobo River, and also the chief town of Dja-et-Lobo, in the South Region of Cameroon. The language spoken there is Bulu.

G2223763.description: Nkongsamba is a city in western Cameroon. It is in the Moungo department, which is in the Littoral.

G2224197.description: Njombé is a town and commune in Cameroon.

G2224827.description: Ngaoundéré or N'Gaoundéré (Fula: N'gamdere, نغَمْدٜرٜ, 𞤲'𞤺𞤢𞤥𞤣𞤫𞥅𞤪𞤫𞥅) is the capital of the Adamawa Region of Cameroon. It had a population of 152,700 at the 2005 census.

G2225325.description: Ndelele is a town and commune in Cameroon. Cameroon is home to many native languages, though the main three being: German, french and English.

G2227402.description: Meiganga (Fula: Meiganga 𞤥𞤫𞤭𞤺𞤢𞤲𞤺𞤢) is a town in the Adamawa Region of Cameroon. It is located at around 6.53°N 14.37°E / 6.53; 14.37.

G2228079.description: Mbalmayo is a town in Cameroon's Centre Region. The town had 60,091 inhabitants in 2012.

G2228373.description: Maroua (Fula: Marwa, مَرْوَ, 𞤥𞤢𞤪𞤱𞤢) is the capital of the Far North Region of Cameroon, stretching along the banks of the Ferngo and Kaliao Rivers, in the foothills of the Mandara Mountains. The city had 201,371 inhabitants at the 2005 census, consisting mainly of the Fulbe/Fulani ethnic group.

G2228902.description: Makak is a town in central Cameroon, in Central province.

G2229411.description: Limbé or Limbe (known as Victoria from 1858 to 1982) is a seaside city in the South-West Region of Cameroon. At the 2005 Census, the population was 84,223.

G2229752.description: Kumba is a city in the Southwest Region of Cameroon and the administrative capital of Meme Division. It is one of the largest and most economically significant cities in the Anglophone regions of Cameroon.

G2229761.description: Kribi is a beach resort and sea port in Cameroon.

G2229798.description: Kousséri (from Arabic: قصور quṣūr meaning "palaces"), founded and known as Mser in the indigenous Mser language, is a city in Far North Province, Cameroon. It is the capital of the Logone-et-Chari department.

G2230876.description: Guider (sometimes spelled Guidder) is a city situated in Cameroon's North Province, close to the border with Chad. It has a population of 400,000.

G2231320.description: Garoua (also Garua; Fula: 𞤺𞤢𞤪𞤱𞤢, Garwa) is a port city and the capital of the North Region of Cameroon, lying on the Benue River. A thriving centre of the textiles and cotton industries, the city has approximately 900,000 inhabitants in 2022, with a significant population of Fulbe/Fulani people.

G2231506.description: Foumban or Fumban is a city in Cameroon, lying north east of Bafoussam. It has a population of 83,522 (at the 2005 Census).

G2232239.description: Edéa is a city and commune in the Littoral Region of Cameroon. Situated on the Sanaga River, it lies on the Douala–Yaoundé–Ngaoundéré railway line.

G2232283.description: Ebolowa is a city in Cameroon. It is the capital of the South Region and the Mvila department.

G2232444.description: Dschang is a city located in the West (Ouest) Province of Cameroon, with an estimated population of 87,000 (est) in 2001, growing dramatically from 21,705 recorded in 1981. The 2006 Population is estimated to be 200,000 inhabitants.

G2232593.description: Douala is the largest city in Cameroon and its economic capital. It is also the capital of Cameroon's Littoral Region.

G2233410.description: Buea is the capital of the Southwest Region of Cameroon. The city is located in Fako Division, on the eastern slopes of Mount Cameroon, and has a population of about 47,300 inhabitants as of 2025.

G2234359.description: Bertoua is a city in Cameroon. It is the capital of the East Region of the Lom-et-Djerem Department.

G2234865.description: Bangangté is a town and commune in Cameroon. It is the capital of the Ndé division of West Region.

G2234974.description: Bamenda, also known as Abakwa and Mankon Town, is a city in northwestern Cameroon and capital of the Northwest Region. The city has a population of about six hundred thousand people and is located 366 km (227 mi) north-west of the Cameroonian capital, Yaoundé.

G2235189.description: Bafoussam is the capital and largest city of the West Region of Cameroon, in the Bamboutos Mountains. It is the 3rd most important (financially) city in Cameroon, after Yaoundé and Douala.
